story.what_it_does: Zensar Technologies is an IT services company. In FY26 it earned INR 56,874 million of revenue and INR 7,746 million of profit after tax. The notes name Banking and Financial Services (BFS/FSI) and Telecom, Media and Technology (TMT) as segments, and Healthcare also appears.
story.plans: Management is pushing AI, with 85% of the workforce AI-certified and AI-influenced deals at 36% of the order book in Q2 FY27. It is ramping up a large deal, which is costing margin early on. Its stated targets include 70% renewable energy by FY30 and net-zero emissions across the value chain by FY45.
story.moat: The notes show no explicit moat statement. Supporting points are a healthy cash pile ($317.5M in Q1 FY27), return on capital employed of 22.7% in FY26, and top-5 clients at about 25% of revenue, so it is not overly concentrated. Attrition is fairly low at about 9-10%.

scenarios.story: The large deal ramps up and margins recover as early costs fade, with EBITDA margin already up from 14.6% to 15.8% in Q2 FY27. Banking keeps growing (17.1%) and AI-led deals add to demand.
signals_to_watch: EBITDA margin moving back toward the 16-17% seen earlier
Order book growing from $151.5M in Q2 FY27

scenarios.story: Revenue grows slowly, as shown by 4.1% sequential constant-currency growth in Q2 FY27 after 1.1% in Q1. Banking strength offsets telecom weakness while margins stay in the mid-teens.

Telecom, Media and Technology keeps shrinking (down 21.6% year on year in constant currency in Q2 FY27) and long client decision cycles drag on demand. Large-deal costs or higher headcount (12,320) could keep profits under pressure.
signals_to_watch: Further falls in Telecom, Media and Technology revenue
Profit after tax growth, which turned negative year on year (-4.0% in constant currency) in Q2 FY27
